name: Machine Shoulder Press
summary: A seated overhead pressing movement performed on a guided machine to develop the shoulders and triceps.

setup: Adjust the seat height so that the handles sit roughly level with your chin or the tops of your shoulders.
Sit back firmly with your upper back and hips supported against the pads.
Plant your feet flat on the floor and grasp the handles with an overhand or neutral grip.
steps: Press the handles smoothly overhead until your arms are extended, stopping just short of locking out your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top while maintaining tension in the shoulders.
Lower the handles under control back to the starting depth around ear or chin level.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the handles and exhale forcefully as you press overhead.
cues: Drive your knuckles to the ceiling.
Keep your back firmly against the pad.
Control the descent; do not bounce off the weight stack.

common_faults.fault: Excessive arching of the lower back to turn the lift into an incline chest press.
common_faults.correction: Keep your core braced and your entire back flat against the seat pad throughout the movement.

common_faults.fault: Seat adjusted too low, forcing the shoulders into extreme, uncomfortable horizontal abduction at the bottom.
common_faults.correction: Raise the seat so the starting position places the handles around chin to shoulder height.

common_faults.fault: Locking out the elbows aggressively at the top of the press.
common_faults.correction: Stop just short of lockout to preserve joint health and maintain continuous tension on the target muscles.

precautions: If shoulder mobility is limited, use neutral handles if available or stop the descent slightly above shoulder level.
